title: How Do Software Development Teams Work?
partialText: Get a sense for how software development teams work together, what various roles are and how they coordinate workloads.

title: A Better v-model with defineModel
partialText: Rather than three separate pieces for a two-way bound value, defineModel gives this common Vue component pattern a single line of syntax.

title: Building Trustworthy AI Experiences
partialText: Providing source attribution, explanations and transparency can help bolster user trust in an AI-powered application.

title: Ready for .NET 11: Day-Zero Support Across the Telerik Portfolio
partialText: The Progress Telerik portfolio of products is ready for .NET 11 support so you won’t miss a step.

title: QR Codes and Barcodes: Real-World Use Cases in Blazor
partialText: See how to use QR codes and barcodes together in a real use case of an event-ticketing Blazor application, plus checking in the ticket at the event.

title: Introducing Server Components in TanStack Start
partialText: This simple app shows how React Server Components work in TanStack Start, how server and client components compose together, and what this means for performance and application design.

title: My Favorite Color Extensions from the .NET MAUI Community Toolkit
partialText: Color Extensions, provided by the .NET MAUI Community Toolkit, give you a way to animate color changes or convert colors in certain situations. Take a look!

title: So the ‘AI Differentiator’ Is Taste … But What IS Taste?
partialText: If the only thing separating our work from AI slop is taste, then our new primary task as developers needs to be figuring out what that means.

title: What Are Memory and Context in AI Agent Observability?
partialText: An AI agent can complete every step successfully and still act on outdated information. Learn what memory and context are, why they matter for AI agents and how traces help pinpoint where information went wrong. See how memory tools help update or remove stale records before they affect another run.

title: Object Calisthenics: 9 Exercises That Will Elevate Your Code Quality
partialText: Object Calisthenics is a set of nine rules that challenges the way we think about and write object-oriented code. See how they can help evolve our code.

title: Designing Dynamic Applications for Users and Agents
partialText: Dynamic applications can adapt workflows in real time as tasks change, reducing user navigation and repetitive input and providing agents with structured paths.

title: Blazor Basics: Persisting Component State in Blazor with .NET 10
partialText: Learn how to reuse state between prerendering and establishing interactivity in Blazor components.

title: Design for Delegation with Progressive Autonomy
partialText: Progressive autonomy for agents works the same as delegating a presentation to a 20-year-old new hire. But full autonomy on day one is maybe not a great idea.

title: Tips for Getting Started with .NET MAUI
partialText: Understand what you’re trying to build before you begin, practice, learn from the community and more advice from a fellow .NET MAUI dev.

title: Introduction to gRPC as a Tool for Connecting Microservices
partialText: Learn how to build and connect to gRPC servers by creating a movie listing microservice. We’ll define an API contract using Protocol Buffers, set up a NestJS gRPC server with streaming support, and connect clients using both grpcurl and .NET.
